interfaces: CommandValidatorSpec { kind: 'command', validatorId, category, required, command, args?, cwd?, timeoutMs?, description? }
FunctionValidatorSpec { kind: 'function', validatorId, category, required, execute, timeoutMs?, description? }
ValidatorResult { validatorId, category, required, executor, status, startedAt, finishedAt, durationMs, diagnostics }
ValidationRunResult { outcome, startedAt, finishedAt, durationMs, results }

behavioralConstraints: the core executor never hard-codes a concrete validator command; every check is supplied by the caller as a ValidatorSpec
validators execute in exactly the order supplied to the constructor and are never reordered, parallelized, or deduplicated beyond rejecting duplicate validatorId values
every validator in a registered set runs even after an earlier validator fails, so one run captures full evidence for the whole set
a command validator's exit code 0 is PASS, a non-zero exit code is FAIL, and a spawn failure or timeout/signal termination is ERROR
a function validator's returned status is used directly; a thrown error, an invalid returned status, or exceeding its declared timeoutMs is ERROR
the aggregate outcome is FAIL only when at least one required validator's status is not PASS; optional (required: false) validators never affect the aggregate outcome
a validator result always includes identity (validatorId, category, required), the concrete executor description, status, ISO start/finish timestamps, duration, and concise diagnostics
invariants: the framework performs no persistence of evidence beyond the returned in-memory ValidationRunResult
the framework does not advance task lifecycle state
the framework performs no AI semantic review
the framework requires no network access to execute or to be tested
ERROR (infrastructure/execution failure) is always distinguishable from FAIL (an assertion the validator itself reported) via the status field
examples: a set of command validators (lint, type-check, tests) all exiting 0 aggregates to PASS
a required command validator exiting non-zero aggregates the run to FAIL while unrelated validators later in the array still execute and report their own status
a command validator that runs longer than its timeoutMs is killed and reported as ERROR with a timeout diagnostic
an optional validator that fails or errors is visible in results but does not flip the aggregate outcome to FAIL
running the same validator array twice produces results in the same validatorId order both times
edgeCases: constructing an executor with zero validators is rejected
registering two validators with the same validatorId is rejected
a command that cannot be spawned (e.g. missing binary) is reported as ERROR rather than throwing out of run()
a function validator returning a status outside PASS/FAIL/ERROR is normalized to ERROR

expectations: each ValidatorResult carries enough identity, outcome, and diagnostic detail to be persisted as validation evidence bound to a task/revision
acceptedRanges: a completed ValidationRunResult with one or more ValidatorResult entries
requiredReachableRanges: a run containing an ERROR result

expectations: the aggregate outcome is authoritative for whether required checks passed
the gate can register task-specific validators without modifying this module's core
